newsitem.title: USA: Diatide cites good P829 data in late trial.
newsitem.headline: Diatide cites good P829 data in late trial.

text.p: Diatide Inc said Tuesday ongoing Phase III trials suggest diagnostic imaging with the company's P829 system reliably rules out malignancies in patients whose X-rays show unexplained nodules on their lungs.
The company said the nodules appear in two percent of chest X-rays and are hard to diagnose without costly needle or surgical biopsies that often produce false-negative results.

It said preliminary results in a trial of its P829 device on 19 lung cancer patients over age 35 at the Arizona Institute of Nuclear Medicine compared favorably with results of transthoracic needle biopsy or a thoracotomy.

"In 18 of the 19 patients, the diagnosis by P829 as to malignancy was identical to the diagnosis using surgical procedures," the company said, giving results at the Society of Nuclear Medicine annual meeting.
More importantly, it said there were no false results in P829 tests, suggesting that the imaging method reliably rules out the presence of malignancy.
Diatide said it expects the trial to end late this year, to be followed soon thereafter with a new drug application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
